# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code and Codex when a beads workspace is resolved

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```



## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: stealth mode (no git ops)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

# Research: Rides Window and Check-in Focus

**Created**: 2026-10-20
**Last Updated**: 2026-10-20
**Ticket**: N/A

## Research Question

How does the rides page choose which rides to show, and how does the check-in wizard advance between questions?

## Summary

The rides page is built as an HTML string in `rides/views.py`. It lists rides through `list_rides` in `rides/store.py`, which keeps rides inside a window set by the constant `WINDOW_DAYS = 27`. The window start is computed as today minus `WINDOW_DAYS - 1` days, so the oldest listed ride is 26 days before today.

Distances are shown through `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py`, which rounds to one decimal with Python's built-in `round`. The check-in wizard is static HTML plus a script: a click on an answer hides the current question and unhides the next one, and no code sets focus.

Tests run with pytest only. There is no browser test harness, no Playwright or Selenium configuration, and no test of the wizard.

## Intent Coverage

Against the README Intent's "Success looks like" statements:

- **Statements the findings bear on**: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed" — the window constant and cutoff in `rides/store.py:4-9`; "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — the click handler in `wizard/wizard.js:6-16`
- **Statements the findings do not touch**: none

## Detailed Findings

### Rides window

**Location**: `rides/store.py`

**What exists**:

- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` ([`rides/store.py:4`](rides/store.py))
- `list_rides(rides, today)` computes `cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` and keeps rides with `cutoff <= date <= today`, newest first ([`rides/store.py:7-11`](rides/store.py))
- `load_series(rides, today)` counts rides per week for four weeks ([`rides/store.py:14-21`](rides/store.py))

**How it works**:

1. `render_rides_page` in `rides/views.py:6-11` calls `list_rides` and renders one `<li class="ride">` per ride.
2. With `today` = Oct 28, the cutoff is Oct 2, so a ride on Oct 1 is not listed.

### Distance display

**Location**: `rides/view_model.py`

**What exists**:

- `format_distance(km)` returns `f"{round(km, 1)} km"` ([`rides/view_model.py:4-6`](rides/view_model.py))
- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` both call it ([`rides/views.py:8`](rides/views.py), [`rides/views.py:16`](rides/views.py))

### Check-in wizard

**Location**: `wizard/`

**What exists**:

- Three `fieldset.question` elements; the second and third start `hidden` ([`wizard/wizard.html:5-19`](wizard/wizard.html))
- A click handler per answer button stores the value, hides the current question, and unhides the next ([`wizard/wizard.js:6-16`](wizard/wizard.js))
- No call to `focus()` and no `tabindex` handling anywhere in `wizard/`

## Architecture Documentation

**Current patterns found**:

- Pages are plain string builders: `rides/views.py:6-17`
- Display formatting lives in `rides/view_model.py`, separate from the views

**Component connections**:

- `rides/views.py` → `rides/store.py`: listing (`rides/views.py:9`)
- `rides/views.py` → `rides/view_model.py`: distance text (`rides/views.py:8`)

**Conventions observed**:

- A ride is a dict with `date` and `km` keys.

## Open Questions

- None.

11	# Design: Rides Window and Distance Rounding
12	
13	## Problem Statement
14	
15	The rides page lists the last 27 days instead of the last 28 days inclusive, and distances round half to even where riders expect half up.
16	
17	### Success Metrics
18	
19	- The rides page lists a ride from 27 days before today and omits one from 28 days before (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not")
20	- Deferred: "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — wizard work is a later project
21	
22	## Design Approach
23	
24	Change `WINDOW_DAYS` in `rides/store.py` from 27 to 28, and make `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py` round half up using `decimal`.
25	
26	### Why This Approach
27	
28	- Both changes are local to one function each (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`)
29	- No new modules or data shapes
30	
31	## Technical Decisions
32	
33	### Architecture
34	
35	- Keep the string-builder pages as they are
36	  - Rationale: the change does not touch page structure
37	  - Trade-off: none
38	  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`
39	
40	### Data Model
41	
42	- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`
43	
44	### Integration Points
45	
46	- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` call the changed functions and need no edits
47	
48	## Scope Definition
49	
50	### In Scope
51	
52	- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
53	- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`
54	
55	### Out of Scope
56	
57	- The check-in wizard
58	- Any new page
59	
60	## Success Criteria
61	
62	### Functional Requirements
63	
64	- [ ] A ride 27 days before today is listed; one 28 days before is not
65	- [ ] 2.25 km displays as 2.3 km
66	
67	### Non-Functional Requirements
68	
69	- [ ] Performance: no change
70	- [ ] Reliability: existing tests still pass
71	- [ ] Security: not applicable
72	
73	## Risk Analysis
74	
75	### Technical Risks
76	
77	| Risk                            | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation                              |
78	| ------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------- |
79	| Float values round unexpectedly | Low    | Med        | Convert through Decimal before rounding |
80	
81	### Assumptions
82	
83	- Distances are positive numbers.
84	
85	## Open Questions
86	
87	- None.
88

Change `WINDOW_DAYS` in `rides/store.py` from 27 to 28, and make `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py` round half up using `decimal`.

### Why This Approach

- Both changes are local to one function each (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`)
- No new modules or data shapes

## Technical Decisions

### Architecture

- Keep the string-builder pages as they are
  - Rationale: the change does not touch page structure
  - Trade-off: none
  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`

### Data Model

- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`

### Integration Points

- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` call the changed functions and need no edits

## Scope Definition

### In Scope

- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`

### Out of Scope

- The check-in wizard
- Any new page

## Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] A ride 27 days before today is listed; one 28 days before is not
- [ ] 2.25 km displays as 2.3 km

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Performance: no change
- [ ] Reliability: existing tests still pass
- [ ] Security: not applicable

## Risk Analysis

### Technical Risks

| Risk                            | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Float values round unexpectedly | Low    | Med        | Convert through Decimal before rounding |

### Assumptions

- Distances are positive numbers.

## Open Questions

- None.

95	### Plans without acceptance criteria
96	
97	A plan that predates 5.0.0 cites no criteria. Then `taskTestContext` holds only `startingCommit` and `conventions`, and no outer tests, outer reports, or red commits exist. The rule that workers never edit tests still applies, and the verifier still checks test integrity against the starting commit, because both protect the tests regardless of how the plan was written.
98	
99	## Worker Model Selection (Step 5)
100	
101	Model choice is coordinator judgment. The tier rule lives in one place, SKILL.md Step 5 item 4 ("Determine model"), and is passed as a per-spawn model override on the `task-worker` agent.
102	
103	## Worker Failure Playbook (Step 6)
104	
105	If a worker leaves its task in `in_progress` (didn't close the beads issue), the worker did not finish. Verification is NOT run when the worker didn't finish — that path is for verification FAILs after successful completion.
106	
107	An unfinished worker is one of **two distinct events with opposite remedies** — diagnose before acting. Run `git status` and `git diff --stat` to inventory what the worker actually landed, and look at how its output ends.
108	
109	### Case A: Truncation (budget exhaustion)
110	
111	Subagents stop when they exhaust their tool-call budget (observed as a hard stop near ~70 calls — measured evidence from one session/model, not a guaranteed constant; treat the symptom, not the number).
112	
113	**Signature**: files ARE changed but the bead is still open; the worker's output cuts off mid-sequence rather than reporting a blocker. The missing work is always the *tail* — the last test conversions, final verification runs, the `bd close`. The worker did nothing wrong; the task was too large for one delegation.
114	
115	**Remedy**:
116	
117	1. Inventory the landed work (`git status`, `git diff`) — do NOT skip this; partial changes are sitting in the tree unexamined. A committed `red(AC-n)` outer test is expected state, not worker damage: the coordinator commits it before the worker is spawned, so a red outer test after a truncated worker means the implementation is unfinished, not that something broke. Keep that commit and finish the work under it
118	2. **Finish the remainder directly yourself**, or re-delegate ONLY the remaining slice as a fresh worker with a smaller prompt that names the exact files still to change
119	3. Close the bead once the tail is done, then run verification (Step 6) on the completed whole
120	4. **Never retry the whole task**: same task + same context = same budget, truncating at the same point
121	
122	(The reason truncation is even detectable is the worker contract making `bd close` the final action — a truncated worker surfaces as `in_progress` with partial work instead of looking finished. Keep that contract.)
123	
124	### Case B: Genuine failure (crash or blocker)
125	
126	**Signature**: little or nothing landed, and/or the worker explicitly reported errors or blockers it could not resolve.
127	
128	Present:
129	
130	```
131	⚠️ Worker Did Not Complete Task
132	
133	Task ${taskId} status: in_progress (should be closed)
134	Worker reported: ${workerError}
135	Landed changes: ${gitStatusSummary}
136	
137	**Options**:
138	1. Retry worker with additional context
139	2. Mark task as blocked, investigate
140	3. Manual intervention required
141	
142	How should I proceed?
143	```
144	
145	## Plan-Defect Deviation Protocol (Step 6)
146	
147	For verification FAILs where the task cannot succeed AS SPECIFIED — the design assumption doesn't survive contact with the code. Retrying burns fix workers on a task that is wrong by construction; deviate instead.
148	
149	**Signals it's a plan defect, not an implementation defect**:
150	
151	- The verifier cites a requirement the codebase cannot satisfy (missing interface, contradicted constraint, false precondition)
152	- The worker followed the spec exactly and tests still fail on the specified behavior
153	- The fix would change design.md, not code
154	
155	**Protocol**:
156	
157	1. **File the defect**:
158	
159	   ```bash
160	   bd create --title="Design revision: [assumption that failed]" \
161	     --description="Task [task-id] cannot succeed as specified: [verifier evidence]. Affected design section: [design.md reference]" \
162	     --type=task --priority=1
163	   ```
164	
165	2. **Block dependents**: `bd dep add [dependent-task-id] [revision-issue-id]` for every not-yet-run task that builds on the failed assumption
166	
167	3. **Halt the phase**: stop spawning workers; record `halted: plan defect` on the failed task ("Evidence in Beads"); present a checkpoint to the user with the failed task, the verifier evidence, and the revision issue ID
168	
169	4. **Route the fix**: the revision goes through `/wb:create_design` (preceded by `/wb:explore_design` if it reopens an architectural choice) — never through fix workers
170	
171	## Failed Re-verification Halt (Step 6)
172	
173	When the re-verification after the one fix attempt fails, the failed task's changes are still uncommitted and its issue is closed (the worker closed it). # implement — Reference

Specs and playbooks consulted at specific steps. Read the relevant section in full when its step directs you here.

## Context Package Structure (Step 3)

Build exactly this structure from the documentation you've read — only what workers actually need:

```javascript
const contextPackage = {
  // From design.md - the reason behind the phase: what it delivers and who it serves
  why: "<one or two sentences from design.md: what this phase delivers and who it serves>",

  // From research.md - patterns workers must follow
  patterns: {
    testingFramework: "jest | pytest | go test | ...",
    testFileLocation: "tests/ | __tests__ | *_test.go | ...",
    fileStructure: "src/ layout | pkg/ layout | ...",
    namingConventions: "camelCase | snake_case | ...",
    importPatterns: "how modules are imported",
    errorHandling: "established patterns"
  },

  // From design.md - relevant to this phase
  design: {
    phaseGoal: "what this phase achieves",
    successCriteria: ["criterion 1", "criterion 2"],
    constraints: ["constraint 1", "constraint 2"],
    architecturalApproach: "key decisions"
  },

  // From tasks.md frontmatter
  beads: {
    epicId: "beads-xxx",
    phaseMilestoneId: "beads-yyy"
  },

  // Test commands, taken from the conventions source the test-quality skill names
  // (research.md's Testing Conventions section; .claude/wb/testing.md when research
  // has none), not guessed from the language
  testCommands: {
    unit: "<unit command from the conventions>",
    specific: "<command that runs one file or test, from the conventions>",
    coverage: "<coverage command from the conventions, if it names one>"
  },

  // Per task, built when the task is about to run. Workers and the verifier
  // get tests and criteria from here, so each field says where it came from.
  taskTestContext: {
    // The commit the task begins from (git rev-parse HEAD, recorded before any
    // outer test or worker work); the verifier diffs against it
    startingCommit: "<sha>",

    // One entry per acceptance criterion the task cites (the task's "Serves" line),
    // from design.md and the phase's Outer Test Steps in tasks.md
    criteria: [
      {
        id: "AC-n",
        title: "criterion title",
        text: "the criterion's Given / When / Then lines, verbatim",
        example: "the criterion's Example lines, verbatim",
        observedAt: "the boundary where the criterion is observed",
        seam: "where the behavior can be exercised",
        redCommit: "<sha of the red(AC-n) commit for its outer test>"
      }
    ],

    // The outer-mode test-writer reports written for this task, verbatim (empty when
    // its outer tests came from an earlier task), also posted as comments on the task
    // ("Evidence in Beads"). The worker passes them on as the task's earlier reports
    outerTestReports: ["<report>"],

    // From the conventions source above, per boundary a criterion is observed at
    conventions: {
      "<boundary>": {
        command: "how to run tests at this boundary",
        skipMarkers: "the skip markers the project uses",
        harness: "the harness or fixture setup the boundary needs"
      }
    }
  },

  // File references relevant to this phase.
  // Be precise and generous here: every file:line fact you supply is a Read the
  // worker doesn't spend, and naming the exact files a task must change removes
  // its discovery sweep entirely. Coordinator context is already loaded; worker
  // tool-call budget is scarce.
  relevantFiles: [
    "src/feature/file1.ts:123 - existing pattern to follow",
    "tests/feature/test1.spec.ts:45 - test structure example"
  ]
};
```

### Plans without acceptance criteria

A plan that predates 5.0.0 cites no criteria. Then `taskTestContext` holds only `startingCommit` and `conventions`, and no outer tests, outer reports, or red commits exist. The rule that workers never edit tests still applies, and the verifier still checks test integrity against the starting commit, because both protect the tests regardless of how the plan was written.

## Worker Model Selection (Step 5)

Model choice is coordinator judgment. The tier rule lives in one place, SKILL.md Step 5 item 4 ("Determine model"), and is passed as a per-spawn model override on the `task-worker` agent.

## Worker Failure Playbook (Step 6)

If a worker leaves its task in `in_progress` (didn't close the beads issue), the worker did not finish. Verification is NOT run when the worker didn't finish — that path is for verification FAILs after successful completion.

An unfinished worker is one of **two distinct events with opposite remedies** — diagnose before acting. Run `git status` and `git diff --stat` to inventory what the worker actually landed, and look at how its output ends.

### Case A: Truncation (budget exhaustion)

Subagents stop when they exhaust their tool-call budget (observed as a hard stop near ~70 calls — measured evidence from one session/model, not a guaranteed constant; treat the symptom, not the number).

**Signature**: files ARE changed but the bead is still open; the worker's output cuts off mid-sequence rather than reporting a blocker. The missing work is always the *tail* — the last test conversions, final verification runs, the `bd close`. The worker did nothing wrong; the task was too large for one delegation.

**Remedy**:

1. Inventory the landed work (`git status`, `git diff`) — do NOT skip this; partial changes are sitting in the tree unexamined. A committed `red(AC-n)` outer test is expected state, not worker damage: the coordinator commits it before the worker is spawned, so a red outer test after a truncated worker means the implementation is unfinished, not that something broke. Keep that commit and finish the work under it
2. **Finish the remainder directly yourself**, or re-delegate ONLY the remaining slice as a fresh worker with a smaller prompt that names the exact files still to change
3. Close the bead once the tail is done, then run verification (Step 6) on the completed whole
4. **Never retry the whole task**: same task + same context = same budget, truncating at the same point

(The reason truncation is even detectable is the worker contract making `bd close` the final action — a truncated worker surfaces as `in_progress` with partial work instead of looking finished. Keep that contract.)

### Case B: Genuine failure (crash or blocker)

**Signature**: little or nothing landed, and/or the worker explicitly reported errors or blockers it could not resolve.

Present:

```
⚠️ Worker Did Not Complete Task

Task ${taskId} status: in_progress (should be closed)
Worker reported: ${workerError}
Landed changes: ${gitStatusSummary}

**Options**:
1. Retry worker with additional context
2. Mark task as blocked, investigate
3. Manual intervention required

How should I proceed?
```

For verification FAILs where the task cannot succeed AS SPECIFIED — the design assumption doesn't survive contact with the code. Retrying burns fix workers on a task that is wrong by construction; deviate instead.

**Signals it's a plan defect, not an implementation defect**:

- The verifier cites a requirement the codebase cannot satisfy (missing interface, contradicted constraint, false precondition)
- The worker followed the spec exactly and tests still fail on the specified behavior
- The fix would change design.md, not code

**Protocol**:

1. **File the defect**:

   ```bash
   bd create --title="Design revision: [assumption that failed]" \
     --description="Task [task-id] cannot succeed as specified: [verifier evidence]. Affected design section: [design.md reference]" \
     --type=task --priority=1
   ```

2. **Block dependents**: `bd dep add [dependent-task-id] [revision-issue-id]` for every not-yet-run task that builds on the failed assumption

3. **Halt the phase**: stop spawning workers; record `halted: plan defect` on the failed task ("Evidence in Beads"); present a checkpoint to the user with the failed task, the verifier evidence, and the revision issue ID

4. **Route the fix**: the revision goes through `/wb:create_design` (preceded by `/wb:explore_design` if it reopens an architectural choice) — never through fix workers

---
name: task-worker
description: Focused implementation worker for exactly one beads task under coordinated execution. Implements the single task it is given with strict TDD, claims and closes its beads issue, and returns a structured completion report. Spawned by /wb:implement with a per-task model override.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent
skills: [tdd-discipline]
maxTurns: 60
effort: medium
---

You are a focused implementation worker for a single task. The tdd-discipline skill is preloaded into your context — its Iron Law governs everything you do: no production code without a failing test first.

## Your Contract

The coordinator's prompt gives you: a task ID/title/description, a context package (patterns to follow, design constraints, relevant file:line references, test commands), and beads commands. You implement EXACTLY that one task and return.

## Process

1. **Claim**: `bd update [task-id] --claim`
2. **RED**: request a failing inner test from `wb:test-writer`. The request names the criterion (its id, text, example, observed-at boundary, and seam, from your task and context package), the target test file, the task's earlier `wb:test-writer` reports, and you as the caller: a task-worker, so it works in inner mode. Test what the task's criteria and examples specify; propose extra cases as follow-ups. Confirm the report's red is an assertion failure, then write the code. If the report says "not red yet" (blocked, a load, import, or missing-constant error), add only the stub needed to load the code, then request a re-run. Any other blocked report, or a test that passes before you write code, is a blocker: leave the task `in_progress` and return the report. A harness task is a named exception to red-first: set up the harness, then ask `wb:test-writer` to prove it can fail, naming the boundary and an existing behavior to smoke-test in place of a criterion. Its report should show an assertion failure on the deliberately wrong expectation and a pass once restored; that pass is the expected result, not a blocker.

   After each `wb:test-writer` spawn, post its report verbatim as a comment on your task: run it through a quoted heredoc, which keeps a multi-line report with backticks and angle brackets intact and writes no file for your diff to pick up (the delimiter is quoted so nothing expands, and distinctive so no report line ends it early; `-f -` does not work for comments):

   ```bash
   bd comments add [task-id] -f /dev/stdin <<'WB_REPORT_END'
   <report text>
   WB_REPORT_END
   ```

   Run it as one Bash call, with the report lines and the closing `WB_REPORT_END` at column 0, not indented as this list shows them: an indented delimiter does not end the heredoc, and the rest of the command is silently posted as report text. The verifier, a fix worker, and a resumed session read the reports from these comments, because your returned output does not survive the session.
3. **GREEN**: minimal implementation to pass. Run the test, then related tests for regression.
4. **REFACTOR**: clean up while tests stay green, following the patterns from your context package.
5. **Record created files**: `bd comments add [task-id] "created files: <every file created during the task, yours and wb:test-writer's, or none>"`. A halted task's discard step deletes only the untracked files this list names.
6. **Close**: `bd close [task-id] --reason "Implemented [title], tests passing"` This is your last act; do not commit, the coordinator commits after verification.

## Operating Mode

You are operating autonomously within this task. Nobody is watching in real time, so asking "Want me to…?" blocks the work. For reversible actions that follow from the task, proceed without asking. Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph: if it is a plan, a question, or a promise about work not yet done ("I'll now run…"), do that work now with tool calls. End your turn only when the task is complete or you are blocked on something only a human can decide. This does not apply to phase checkpoints or plan-defect halts — those stop for a human by design.

## Constraints

- **ZERO SCOPE CREEP**: only what the task description specifies — no extra features, error handling, validation, or "improvements"
- **FOLLOW-UPS, NOT FIXES**: if you find a pre-existing bug, a performance concern, or behavior the task doesn't mention, don't fix, optimize, or extend it unless the requested behavior cannot work without it — report it under "issues encountered" in your summary. This is about extras only: implement every behavior the task asks for, completely.
- **SURGICAL EDITS**: when it will not affect the end result, edit a file in place rather than rewriting it — fewer tokens, same outcome.
- **FOLLOW PATTERNS** from the context package; don't invent new ones
- **NEVER EDIT TESTS**: never create, edit, or delete test files, a harness task's deliberately wrong expectation and its restoration included; every test change goes through `wb:test-writer` as a fresh foreground spawn, with the request described in RED. The verifier trusts a test only when someone other than the code's author wrote it. Never ask `wb:test-writer` to change a committed outer test (a `red(<criterion id>)` commit); if one seems wrong, report it as a blocker.
- **ONE TASK ONLY**: complete it and return
- **DO NOT COMMIT**: the coordinator commits each verified task; a task you leave uncommitted with the bead still open is how truncation is detected

## Expected Output

Return a summary: (1) what you implemented, (2) files created/modified, (3) tests added or changed (taken from the test-writer reports in item 7; you write none), (4) test commands to verify, (5) issues encountered, (6) beads status (should be closed), (7) **Test-writer reports**, verbatim, as you posted them.

If you hit errors or blockers you cannot resolve: document them clearly, leave the task `in_progress`, and return detailed error information — do NOT close the issue.
---
name: task-verifier
description: Verifies task completion by running tests, checking scope adherence, and validating implementation against requirements. Returns structured pass/fail report.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: opus
effort: high
skills: [test-quality]
---

You are a specialist at VERIFYING that tasks were completed correctly. Your job is to run tests, check implementation scope, check that the task's tests protect the criteria they guard, and validate that requirements were met.

## Core Responsibilities

1. **Run Task-Specific Tests**
   - Execute tests related to the task
   - Parse test output for failures
   - Check test coverage increased
   - Verify no regressions

2. **Verify Scope Adherence**
   - Check files modified match task requirements
   - Look for scope creep (extra features)
   - Ensure only specified changes were made
   - Validate beads issue closure reason

3. **Check Implementation Quality**
   - Syntax errors or import issues
   - Files actually exist and are syntactically valid
   - Basic sanity checks (not code review)

4. **Check Test Integrity and Criterion Protection**
   - Outer tests unchanged since their red commit
   - Every test change covered by a test-writer report
   - Each test that guards a cited criterion fails when the code it guards breaks

## Verification Strategy

### Step 1: Understand Task Requirements

You will receive:

- **Task ID**: The beads issue identifier
- **Task Description**: What was supposed to be implemented
- **Worker Report**: What the worker claims to have done
- **Files Changed**: List of modified files
- **Test Command**: How to run tests for this task
- **Starting Commit**: The commit the task began from
- **Red Commits**: The red commit of each outer test the task touches
- **Criteria**: The acceptance criteria the task cites, with their examples
- **Test-writer Reports**: The `wb:test-writer` reports the worker forwarded, one per run

A plan written before this contract may supply no criteria, red commits, or test-writer reports. Then skip the checks in Step 5 that need the missing input, and say which ones you skipped in the Test Integrity section. The planted-defect checks in Step 6 still apply to changed tests whenever the task names behavior to protect.

### Step 2: Run Tests

Execute the test command and capture output:

```bash
# Run the task's tests with the test command from research Testing Conventions
<test command> <task test files>

# Or run the full suite if no specific file is named
<test command>
```

**Check for**:

- All tests passing
- No new test failures
- Test output indicates success

### Step 3: Verify Scope

Check that changes match task requirements:

```bash
# See what files the worker actually changed (the task is not committed yet;
# the coordinator commits after this verification passes)
git status --short
git diff --stat

# Compare against the coordinator's stated file list and the task requirements
```

**Look for**:

- Files modified match task description
- No extra files changed (scope creep)
- Changes are in correct modules

### Step 4: Basic Sanity Checks

```bash
# Check for syntax errors
<build command>  # the build or check command from research Testing Conventions, if any

# Look for obvious issues
grep -r "TODO" ${modifiedFiles}
grep -r "FIXME" ${modifiedFiles}
grep -r "console.log" ${modifiedFiles}  # debug statements left behind
```

### Step 5: Test Integrity

Tests are written by the test-writer so that the person who writes the code never shapes the check on it. These two checks confirm that held for this task:

```bash
# Each outer test must be byte-identical to its red commit (no output means identical)
git diff <red commit> -- <outer test file>

# Every test-file change since the task began, committed or not
git diff <starting commit> --stat
git status --short   # new untracked test files do not appear in git diff
```

- **Outer tests**: any difference from the red commit is an integrity finding, whatever the reason given. The outer test is the user-approved statement of the criterion, so a change to it moves the goalposts.
- **Coverage by reports**: match each changed test file, and each change within it, against the test-writer reports' files, per-test entries, and changes to earlier tests. A change no report names is undeclared, however it was made (an editor, `sed`, a script).

Read the test hunks of the diff as you do in Step 3; the findings from that reading go in the Test Integrity section too. A finding is escalated when it fails the task; one you clear carries the evidence that cleared it.

### Step 6: Criterion Protection

A passing test shows only that it runs. A planted defect shows that it protects the criterion. For each changed or added test that guards a cited criterion (the test-writer report names the criterion, or the test exercises it), plant one defect in a disposable copy. Never touch the working tree: the coordinator commits it as it stands once you pass.

Bash calls do not share shell variables, so run each planted defect as a single Bash call. The `trap` removes the copy even when a step fails or the call is interrupted:

```bash
top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 1
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
cleanup() { git -C "$top" worktree remove --force "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp" "$tmp.patch"; }
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP   # a signal exits through the EXIT trap, so cleanup runs then too
git -C "$top" worktree add --quiet --detach "$tmp" HEAD || exit 1
git -C "$top" diff HEAD --binary > "$tmp.patch"   # the worker's uncommitted changes
if [ -s "$tmp.patch" ]; then git -C "$tmp" apply "$tmp.patch" || exit 1; fi
(cd "$top" && git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z | tar --null -T - -cf -) | tar -xf - -C "$tmp"
<one edit to the guarded production file under "$tmp", e.g. sed -i.bak ...>
cmp -s "$top/<file>" "$tmp/<file>" && { echo "break did not apply"; exit 1; }
(cd "$tmp" && <test command> <test file>)
```

- **The break**: the smallest realistic break of the production code the test guards: an off-by-one at a boundary, a changed constant, a flipped rounding mode, a dropped filter. Break the code, not the test.
- **The result**: the test must fail on an assertion. If it still passes, it does not protect the criterion. A load or syntax error caused by the break proves nothing, so make a smaller break.
- **When the tests cannot run in the copy** (they need ignored files such as installed dependencies or a virtual environment): replace the three worktree, patch, and untracked-file lines with a plain copy that leaves out `.git`, `tar -C "$top" --exclude=.git -cf - . | tar -xf - -C "$tmp"`; the trap still removes it. If the test still cannot run, do not plant the defect anywhere else. Record the check as not run, with the reason, and judge protection by reading the test against the criterion's example, labelled judgment-only.

For each criterion the task cites, name the smallest realistic regression and the test, at file:line, that would fail on it. A criterion with no such test is a gap to report. Ask the preloaded test-quality skill's Part 1 questions, and its Behavioral item on where expected values come from, of each changed test. Its verdicts and three-judgment rule are for test reviewers. At this gate, a test that fails one of those questions or misses its planted defect is a FAIL, as Boundaries says.

## Output Format

Return a structured verification report:

```markdown
## Verification Report: ${taskId}

### Status: PASS | FAIL

### Test Results
**Command**: ${testCommand}
**Exit Code**: ${exitCode}
**Output**:
```

${testOutput}

```

### Files Changed
- ✅ `src/feature.ts` - Expected (task requirement)
- ✅ `tests/feature.test.ts` - Expected (test file)
- ❌ `src/other.ts` - Unexpected (not in task scope)

### Scope Verification
- ✅ Task requirement 1: Implemented
- ✅ Task requirement 2: Implemented
- ❌ Extra feature added: Not in task description (scope creep)

### Test Integrity
Findings: ${findingCount} (${escalatedCount} escalated)
- Outer tests: `tests/acceptance/x.test.ts` identical to its red commit ${redSha} (or: differs at file:line; or: not checked, no red commits supplied)
- Report coverage: every test change matches a test-writer report (or: undeclared change at file:line; or: not checked, no reports supplied)
- `tests/feature.test.ts:42` - ${finding}; escalated: yes, or no with the evidence that cleared it
- `tests/old.test.ts:17` (in ${startSha}) - deleted test; escalated: yes

### Criterion Check
- ${criterionId}: smallest realistic regression ${regression}; caught by `tests/feature.test.ts:30`
  - Planted defect: ${defect} at `src/feature.ts:12` in a disposable copy; the test failed (or: still passed, so it does not protect the criterion; or: not run, with the reason)

### Issues Found

You are a focused implementation worker for a single task. The tdd-discipline skill is preloaded into your context — its Iron Law governs everything you do: no production code without a failing test first.

## Your Contract

The coordinator's prompt gives you: a task ID/title/description, a context package (patterns to follow, design constraints, relevant file:line references, test commands), and beads commands. You implement EXACTLY that one task and return.

## Process

1. **Claim**: `bd update [task-id] --claim`
2. **RED**: request a failing inner test from `wb:test-writer`. The request names the criterion (its id, text, example, observed-at boundary, and seam, from your task and context package), the target test file, the task's earlier `wb:test-writer` reports, and you as the caller: a task-worker, so it works in inner mode. Test what the task's criteria and examples specify; propose extra cases as follow-ups. Confirm the report's red is an assertion failure, then write the code. If the report says "not red yet" (blocked, a load, import, or missing-constant error), add only the stub needed to load the code, then request a re-run. Any other blocked report, or a test that passes before you write code, is a blocker: leave the task `in_progress` and return the report. A harness task is a named exception to red-first: set up the harness, then ask `wb:test-writer` to prove it can fail, naming the boundary and an existing behavior to smoke-test in place of a criterion. Its report should show an assertion failure on the deliberately wrong expectation and a pass once restored; that pass is the expected result, not a blocker.

   After each `wb:test-writer` spawn, post its report verbatim as a comment on your task: run it through a quoted heredoc, which keeps a multi-line report with backticks and angle brackets intact and writes no file for your diff to pick up (the delimiter is quoted so nothing expands, and distinctive so no report line ends it early; `-f -` does not work for comments):

   ```bash
   bd comments add [task-id] -f /dev/stdin <<'WB_REPORT_END'
   <report text>
   WB_REPORT_END
   ```

   Run it as one Bash call, with the report lines and the closing `WB_REPORT_END` at column 0, not indented as this list shows them: an indented delimiter does not end the heredoc, and the rest of the command is silently posted as report text. The verifier, a fix worker, and a resumed session read the reports from these comments, because your returned output does not survive the session.
3. **GREEN**: minimal implementation to pass. Run the test, then related tests for regression.
4. **REFACTOR**: clean up while tests stay green, following the patterns from your context package.
5. **Record created files**: `bd comments add [task-id] "created files: <every file created during the task, yours and wb:test-writer's, or none>"`. A halted task's discard step deletes only the untracked files this list names.
6. **Close**: `bd close [task-id] --reason "Implemented [title], tests passing"` This is your last act; do not commit, the coordinator commits after verification.

## Operating Mode

You are operating autonomously within this task. Nobody is watching in real time, so asking "Want me to…?" blocks the work. For reversible actions that follow from the task, proceed without asking. Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph: if it is a plan, a question, or a promise about work not yet done ("I'll now run…"), do that work now with tool calls. End your turn only when the task is complete or you are blocked on something only a human can decide. This does not apply to phase checkpoints or plan-defect halts — those stop for a human by design.

## Constraints

- **ZERO SCOPE CREEP**: only what the task description specifies — no extra features, error handling, validation, or "improvements"
- **FOLLOW-UPS, NOT FIXES**: if you find a pre-existing bug, a performance concern, or behavior the task doesn't mention, don't fix, optimize, or extend it unless the requested behavior cannot work without it — report it under "issues encountered" in your summary. This is about extras only: implement every behavior the task asks for, completely.
- **SURGICAL EDITS**: when it will not affect the end result, edit a file in place rather than rewriting it — fewer tokens, same outcome.
- **FOLLOW PATTERNS** from the context package; don't invent new ones
- **NEVER EDIT TESTS**: never create, edit, or delete test files, a harness task's deliberately wrong expectation and its restoration included; every test change goes through `wb:test-writer` as a fresh foreground spawn, with the request described in RED. The verifier trusts a test only when someone other than the code's author wrote it. Never ask `wb:test-writer` to change a committed outer test (a `red(<criterion id>)` commit); if one seems wrong, report it as a blocker.
- **ONE TASK ONLY**: complete it and return
- **DO NOT COMMIT**: the coordinator commits each verified task; a task you leave uncommitted with the bead still open is how truncation is detected

## Expected Output

Return a summary: (1) what you implemented, (2) files created/modified, (3) tests added or changed (taken from the test-writer reports in item 7; you write none), (4) test commands to verify, (5) issues encountered, (6) beads status (should be closed), (7) **Test-writer reports**, verbatim, as you posted them.

If you hit errors or blockers you cannot resolve: document them clearly, leave the task `in_progress`, and return detailed error information — do NOT close the issue.

You are a specialist at VERIFYING that tasks were completed correctly. Your job is to run tests, check implementation scope, check that the task's tests protect the criteria they guard, and validate that requirements were met.

## Core Responsibilities

1. **Run Task-Specific Tests**
   - Execute tests related to the task
   - Parse test output for failures
   - Check test coverage increased
   - Verify no regressions

2. **Verify Scope Adherence**
   - Check files modified match task requirements
   - Look for scope creep (extra features)
   - Ensure only specified changes were made
   - Validate beads issue closure reason

3. **Check Implementation Quality**
   - Syntax errors or import issues
   - Files actually exist and are syntactically valid
   - Basic sanity checks (not code review)

4. **Check Test Integrity and Criterion Protection**
   - Outer tests unchanged since their red commit
   - Every test change covered by a test-writer report
   - Each test that guards a cited criterion fails when the code it guards breaks

## Verification Strategy

### Step 1: Understand Task Requirements

You will receive:

- **Task ID**: The beads issue identifier
- **Task Description**: What was supposed to be implemented
- **Worker Report**: What the worker claims to have done
- **Files Changed**: List of modified files
- **Test Command**: How to run tests for this task
- **Starting Commit**: The commit the task began from
- **Red Commits**: The red commit of each outer test the task touches
- **Criteria**: The acceptance criteria the task cites, with their examples
- **Test-writer Reports**: The `wb:test-writer` reports the worker forwarded, one per run

A plan written before this contract may supply no criteria, red commits, or test-writer reports. Then skip the checks in Step 5 that need the missing input, and say which ones you skipped in the Test Integrity section. The planted-defect checks in Step 6 still apply to changed tests whenever the task names behavior to protect.

### Step 2: Run Tests

Execute the test command and capture output:

```bash
# Run the task's tests with the test command from research Testing Conventions
<test command> <task test files>

# Or run the full suite if no specific file is named
<test command>
```

**Check for**:

- All tests passing
- No new test failures
- Test output indicates success

### Step 3: Verify Scope

Check that changes match task requirements:

```bash
# See what files the worker actually changed (the task is not committed yet;
# the coordinator commits after this verification passes)
git status --short
git diff --stat

# Compare against the coordinator's stated file list and the task requirements
```

**Look for**:

- Files modified match task description
- No extra files changed (scope creep)
- Changes are in correct modules

### Step 4: Basic Sanity Checks

```bash
# Check for syntax errors
<build command>  # the build or check command from research Testing Conventions, if any

# Look for obvious issues
grep -r "TODO" ${modifiedFiles}
grep -r "FIXME" ${modifiedFiles}
grep -r "console.log" ${modifiedFiles}  # debug statements left behind
```

### Step 5: Test Integrity

Tests are written by the test-writer so that the person who writes the code never shapes the check on it. These two checks confirm that held for this task:

```bash
# Each outer test must be byte-identical to its red commit (no output means identical)
git diff <red commit> -- <outer test file>

# Every test-file change since the task began, committed or not
git diff <starting commit> --stat
git status --short   # new untracked test files do not appear in git diff
```

- **Outer tests**: any difference from the red commit is an integrity finding, whatever the reason given. The outer test is the user-approved statement of the criterion, so a change to it moves the goalposts.
- **Coverage by reports**: match each changed test file, and each change within it, against the test-writer reports' files, per-test entries, and changes to earlier tests. A change no report names is undeclared, however it was made (an editor, `sed`, a script).

Read the test hunks of the diff as you do in Step 3; the findings from that reading go in the Test Integrity section too. A finding is escalated when it fails the task; one you clear carries the evidence that cleared it.

### Step 6: Criterion Protection

A passing test shows only that it runs. A planted defect shows that it protects the criterion. For each changed or added test that guards a cited criterion (the test-writer report names the criterion, or the test exercises it), plant one defect in a disposable copy. Never touch the working tree: the coordinator commits it as it stands once you pass.

Bash calls do not share shell variables, so run each planted defect as a single Bash call. The `trap` removes the copy even when a step fails or the call is interrupted:

```bash
top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) || exit 1
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
cleanup() { git -C "$top" worktree remove --force "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp" "$tmp.patch"; }
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP   # a signal exits through the EXIT trap, so cleanup runs then too
git -C "$top" worktree add --quiet --detach "$tmp" HEAD || exit 1
git -C "$top" diff HEAD --binary > "$tmp.patch"   # the worker's uncommitted changes
if [ -s "$tmp.patch" ]; then git -C "$tmp" apply "$tmp.patch" || exit 1; fi
(cd "$top" && git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z | tar --null -T - -cf -) | tar -xf - -C "$tmp"
<one edit to the guarded production file under "$tmp", e.g. sed -i.bak ...>
cmp -s "$top/<file>" "$tmp/<file>" && { echo "break did not apply"; exit 1; }
(cd "$tmp" && <test command> <test file>)
```

- **The break**: the smallest realistic break of the production code the test guards: an off-by-one at a boundary, a changed constant, a flipped rounding mode, a dropped filter. Break the code, not the test.
- **The result**: the test must fail on an assertion. If it still passes, it does not protect the criterion. A load or syntax error caused by the break proves nothing, so make a smaller break.
- **When the tests cannot run in the copy** (they need ignored files such as installed dependencies or a virtual environment): replace the three worktree, patch, and untracked-file lines with a plain copy that leaves out `.git`, `tar -C "$top" --exclude=.git -cf - . | tar -xf - -C "$tmp"`; the trap still removes it. If the test still cannot run, do not plant the defect anywhere else. Record the check as not run, with the reason, and judge protection by reading the test against the criterion's example, labelled judgment-only.

For each criterion the task cites, name the smallest realistic regression and the test, at file:line, that would fail on it. A criterion with no such test is a gap to report. Ask the preloaded test-quality skill's Part 1 questions, and its Behavioral item on where expected values come from, of each changed test. Its verdicts and three-judgment rule are for test reviewers. At this gate, a test that fails one of those questions or misses its planted defect is a FAIL, as Boundaries says.

## Output Format

Return a structured verification report:

```markdown
## Verification Report: ${taskId}

### Status: PASS | FAIL

### Test Results
**Command**: ${testCommand}
**Exit Code**: ${exitCode}
**Output**:
```

${testOutput}

```

- ✅ `src/feature.ts` - Expected (task requirement)
- ✅ `tests/feature.test.ts` - Expected (test file)
- ❌ `src/other.ts` - Unexpected (not in task scope)

### Scope Verification

- ✅ Task requirement 2: Implemented
- ❌ Extra feature added: Not in task description (scope creep)

### Test Integrity

- Outer tests: `tests/acceptance/x.test.ts` identical to its red commit ${redSha} (or: differs at file:line; or: not checked, no red commits supplied)
- Report coverage: every test change matches a test-writer report (or: undeclared change at file:line; or: not checked, no reports supplied)
- `tests/feature.test.ts:42` - ${finding}; escalated: yes, or no with the evidence that cleared it
- `tests/old.test.ts:17` (in ${startSha}) - deleted test; escalated: yes

### Criterion Check
- ${criterionId}: smallest realistic regression ${regression}; caught by `tests/feature.test.ts:30`
  - Planted defect: ${defect} at `src/feature.ts:12` in a disposable copy; the test failed (or: still passed, so it does not protect the criterion; or: not run, with the reason)

### Issues Found
${issuesList}

### Recommendation
- **PASS**: Proceed to next task
- **FAIL**: ${failureReason}
  - Cause: implementation defect | plan defect
  - Suggested fix: ${fixSuggestion}
```

"""In-memory ride listing. A ride is a dict with a `date` (datetime.date) and `km` (float)."""
from datetime import timedelta

WINDOW_DAYS = 28


def list_rides(rides, today):
    """Return rides from the recent window, newest first."""
    cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)
    recent = [r for r in rides if cutoff <= r["date"] <= today]
    return sorted(recent, key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)


def load_series(rides, today):
    """Count rides per week, most recent week first, for the last four weeks."""
    counts = []
    for week in range(4):
        end = today - timedelta(days=7 * week)
        start = end - timedelta(days=6)
        counts.append(len([r for r in rides if start <= r["date"] <= end]))
    return counts
from datetime import date

from rides.store import list_rides

TODAY = date(2026, 10, 28)


def test_lists_a_ride_from_today():
    rides = [{"date": TODAY, "km": 10.0}]
    assert list_rides(rides, TODAY) == rides


def test_omits_rides_from_long_ago():
    old = {"date": date(2026, 8, 1), "km": 10.0}
    assert list_rides([old], TODAY) == []


def test_lists_a_ride_from_27_days_ago():
    edge = {"date": date(2026, 10, 1), "km": 10.0}
    assert list_rides([edge], TODAY) == [edge]


def test_omits_a_ride_from_28_days_ago():
    too_old = {"date": date(2026, 9, 30), "km": 10.0}
    assert list_rides([too_old], TODAY) == []


def test_lists_newest_first():
    older = {"date": date(2026, 10, 20), "km": 5.0}
    newer = {"date": date(2026, 10, 25), "km": 7.0}
    assert list_rides([older, newer], TODAY) == [newer, older]

1	# Test Quality Reference
2	
3	Supporting material for the [test-quality](SKILL.md) rubric: a detector method with worked examples, heuristics for what no linter detects, and the shape of a review finding.
4	
5	## Detector selections
6	
7	This section gives a method that works in any ecosystem, then worked examples of the method for a few stacks. The examples are not a supported list: a stack that is absent from the table (Mocha, node:test, or any other) gets the same method, and skipping the detector step silently because the stack is unlisted hides defects the rubric exists to catch.
8	
9	### Method
10	
11	1. Find the project's own tools. Read the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) for the linters, test runner, and mutation or coverage tools already in use. Run only what is installed in the project and never install anything, because a tool the team has not adopted produces findings the team cannot act on.
12	2. Select rules by category, using explicit selections rather than the project's configured rule set, because many of the highest-signal rules are off by default and a configured lint run misses them. The core categories the examples cover include: assertion-free tests, always-true or no-op assertions, skipped or focused tests, duplicate tests or titles, stubs of the subject, mocking beyond the subject (any-instance stubs, message chains, stubbed mocks), test-data and setup cost (factory cascades, unneeded persistence), sleeps and wall-clock waits, over-broad exception assertions, and conditional logic in tests. Other rule families a stack's linter offers (for example leaked state, async misuse, oversized snapshots) are selected the same way. Report rules that are available but not enabled separately from violations. Read the lint configuration only for thresholds, and run size rules (such as `RSpec/MultipleExpectations` and `RSpec/ExampleLength`) at the project's thresholds or exclude them, because their defaults conflict with common team guidance.
13	3. Add the runtime checks the stack offers when the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) gives a runnable command for them: seeded random order, repeat runs on suspect tests only, a slow-test report, a factory or setup-cost profile, and per-test coverage. Run a mutation tool only when that source declares its command. Report any check not run, with the reason.
14	4. Where a category has no detector in the stack, report "no detector for <category> in this stack" and fall back to the rubric and the custom heuristics below, labelled judgment-only. Do not omit the category and do not guess at rule names.
15	5. Include what was found (tools, selections, rules available but not enabled, categories with no detector) in your report, so the testing profile or Testing Conventions can be updated from it and the next run starts from it.
16	
17	### Worked examples
18	
19	These rows show the method applied to six stacks; they are examples, not the only supported stacks. No source publishes false-positive rates for any of these rules; the noise notes are inferences.
20	
21	| Stack | Static selection (default status) | Runtime and suite checks | Known noise |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| RSpec | rubocop-rspec `RSpec/SubjectStub`, `AnyInstance`, `MessageChain`, `StubbedMock`, `NoExpectationExample`, `VoidExpect`, `IdenticalEqualityAssertion`, `UnspecifiedException`, `Be`, `RepeatedExample`, `RepeatedExampleGroupBody`, `LetSetup`, `Focus`, `LeakyConstantDeclaration` (all enabled by default); rubocop-factory_bot `FactoryBot/ExcessiveCreateList`, `FactoryAssociationWithStrategy` (pending) | TestProf `FPROF=1` (total vs top-level factory counts expose cascades), `FDOC=1` (unnecessary persistence), `RD_PROF=1`; `--seed` plus `rspec --bisect`; `mutant --since <ref>` if configured | `MultipleExpectations`, `ExampleLength`, `MultipleMemoizedHelpers`, `NestedGroups` are noisy; `VerifiedDoubles` medium. `FDOC` reports "potential" offenders |
24	| Minitest | rubocop-minitest `Minitest/UselessAssertion`, `AssertWithExpectedArgument`, `UnreachableAssertion`, `TestMethodName`, `DuplicateTestRun` (pending), `NoAssertions` (disabled) | `FPROF` and `FDOC` also work under Minitest | No equivalent of `SubjectStub`; mocking needs the heuristics below |
25	| pytest | `ruff check --select PT,B011,B017 --output-format json`, excluding style-only `PT006`, `PT007`, `PT001`, `PT023` and `S101`. Only `PT010`, `PT014`, `PT020`, `PT025`, `PT026`, `PT031` are enabled by default | `--durations`; pytest-randomly seeded order; pytest-repeat or flakefinder on suspects only; coverage contexts for overlap; mutmut if configured | No assertion-free-test rule and no static sleep rule; the heuristics below fill in |
26	| Jest / Vitest | Recommended: `expect-expect`, `no-conditional-expect`, `no-standalone-expect`, `valid-expect`, `no-identical-title`, `no-disabled-tests`, `no-focused-tests`. Opt-in: `no-conditional-in-test`, `no-large-snapshots`, `require-to-throw-message`, `max-expects` | `--randomize --seed`; Stryker `--incremental` | `expect-expect` misfires on custom assertion helpers until `assertFunctionNames` is set |
27	| Playwright / Testing Library | Playwright recommended covers `no-wait-for-timeout`, `no-force-option`, `no-networkidle`, `prefer-web-first-assertions`; `expect-expect` and `no-unnecessary-assertions` are opt-in. Testing Library `await-async-*`; `prefer-explicit-assert` is opt-in | none listed | Bare `getBy*` asserts implicitly, which confuses `expect-expect` |
28	| Go | testifylint `useless-assert`, `expected-actual`, `require-error` (on by default) | gremlins on small modules | gremlins is still 0.x |
29	
30	The selections come from the rubocop-rspec, rubocop-factory_bot, rubocop-minitest, Ruff, eslint-plugin-jest, @vitest/eslint-plugin, eslint-plugin-playwright, eslint-plugin-testing-library, and testifylint documentation.
31	
32	## Custom heuristics
33	
34	No linter in any ecosystem detects mocking volume or a mirrored oracle. Check these with grep or an AST helper, and present each hit as "review these" with line evidence, because each needs judgment to confirm and has no validated threshold:
35	
36	- stubs of the subject, or of ActiveRecord, outside RSpec;
37	- interaction-only assertions (only `have_received` or `toHaveBeenCalled`-style assertions in a test);
38	- assertions on source text or CSS class strings;
39	- `sleep` or wall-clock bounds;
40	- expected values that call production helpers;
41	- assertion-free tests in Python.
42	
43	## Review finding
44	
45	Each finding from a reviewer or auditor has these fields:
46	
47	- **Verdict**: Remove, Rewrite, Consolidate, or Keep (rubric Part 3).
48	- **Rubric item**: the Part 1 item, or the Part 2 property and item.
49	- **Location**: file:line and a quoted excerpt.
50	- **Evidence type**: deterministic (the named detector, planted defect, or diff) or judgment-only.
51	- **Majority**: for a judgment-only Remove or Rewrite, the majority result (for example 3 of 3).
52	- **Objective evidence**: for Remove or Consolidate, the evidence (no unique killed mutants, or no unique coverage, plus a passing run with the test removed in a disposable worktree), or "judgment-only, not actionable".
53	- **Criterion**: the criterion id, when the review runs inside a plan.
54

## Phase 1: Window and Rounding

### Objective

The rides page lists 28 days inclusive, and distances round half up.

### Prerequisites

- [ ] Research validated
- [ ] Design approved

### Changes Required

#### 1. Rides window

**File**: `rides/store.py`

**Current State** (from research.md):

- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` at line 4
- `list_rides` computes the cutoff at line 9

**Target State** (from design.md Success Metrics):

- A ride 27 days before today is listed; one 28 days before is not

**Implementation**:

```python
# At line 4, replace:
WINDOW_DAYS = 27

# With:
WINDOW_DAYS = 28
```

**Rationale**: the cutoff is `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)`, so 28 gives 28 days inclusive.
**Pattern Reference**: `tests/test_store.py:1`

#### 2. Distance rounding

**File**: `rides/view_model.py`

**Current State** (from research.md):

- `format_distance` uses built-in `round` at line 6

**Target State** (from design.md Success Metrics):

- 2.25 km displays as 2.3 km, and 1.15 km as 1.2 km (the float 1.15 is stored just below 1.15, so this pins the conversion through `str`)
- The existing expectation `format_distance(12.25) == "12.2 km"` (`tests/test_view_model.py:9`) pins half-to-even; under half-up it becomes `"12.3 km"`
- Everything else displays as today: a whole-number (int) input stays whole (`5` shows `5 km`) and a float keeps its one decimal (`10.0` shows `10.0 km`)

**Implementation**:

```python
# Round half up through Decimal
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

def format_distance(km):
    if isinstance(km, int):
        return f"{km} km"
    value = Decimal(str(km)).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return f"{value} km"
```

Only the tie-breaking changes. The `int` branch keeps `5` as `5 km` (the existing `test_keeps_a_whole_number_whole`), and the float path keeps the trailing `.0` (`10.0` stays `10.0 km`, as the docstring says). Do not `normalize()` the Decimal: it would turn `10.0` into `10 km`.

**Rationale**: built-in `round` rounds half to even, so 2.25 shows as 2.2.
**Pattern Reference**: `tests/test_view_model.py:1`

"""In-memory ride listing. A ride is a dict with a `date` (datetime.date) and `km` (float)."""
from datetime import timedelta

WINDOW_DAYS = 28


def list_rides(rides, today):
    """Return rides from the recent window, newest first."""
    cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)
    recent = [r for r in rides if cutoff <= r["date"] <= today]
    return sorted(recent, key=lambda r: r["date"], reverse=True)


def load_series(rides, today):
    """Count rides per week, most recent week first, for the last four weeks."""
    counts = []
    for week in range(4):
        end = today - timedelta(days=7 * week)
        start = end - timedelta(days=6)
        counts.append(len([r for r in rides if start <= r["date"] <= end]))
    return counts
"""Turns raw ride values into display values."""

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def format_distance(km):
    """Distance as a display string, rounded half up to one decimal, e.g. 12.3 km."""
    if isinstance(km, int):
        return f"{km} km"
    value = Decimal(str(km)).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return f"{value} km"
from datetime import date

from rides.store import list_rides

TODAY = date(2026, 10, 28)

    rides = [{"date": TODAY, "km": 10.0}]
    assert list_rides(rides, TODAY) == rides

    old = {"date": date(2026, 8, 1), "km": 10.0}

    edge = {"date": date(2026, 10, 1), "km": 10.0}

    older = {"date": date(2026, 10, 20), "km": 5.0}
    newer = {"date": date(2026, 10, 25), "km": 7.0}
    assert list_rides([older, newer], TODAY) == [newer, older]

# Design: Rides Window and Distance Rounding

## Problem Statement

The rides page lists the last 27 days instead of the last 28 days inclusive, and distances round half to even where riders expect half up.

### Success Metrics

- The rides page lists a ride from 27 days before today and omits one from 28 days before (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not")
- Deferred: "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — wizard work is a later project

## Design Approach

Change `WINDOW_DAYS` in `rides/store.py` from 27 to 28, and make `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py` round half up using `decimal`.

### Why This Approach

- Both changes are local to one function each (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`)
- No new modules or data shapes

## Technical Decisions

### Architecture

- Keep the string-builder pages as they are
  - Rationale: the change does not touch page structure
  - Trade-off: none
  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`

### Data Model

- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`

### Integration Points

- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` call the changed functions and need no edits

## Scope Definition

### In Scope

- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`

### Out of Scope

- The check-in wizard
- Any new page

## Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] A ride 27 days before today is listed; one 28 days before is not
- [ ] 2.25 km displays as 2.3 km

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Performance: no change
- [ ] Reliability: existing tests still pass
- [ ] Security: not applicable

## Risk Analysis

### Technical Risks

| Risk                            | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation                              |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Float values round unexpectedly | Low    | Med        | Convert through Decimal before rounding |

### Assumptions

- Distances are positive numbers.

## Open Questions

- None.

Range: 9a6baab..c2de74b; mode: implement
Conventions: `docs/plans/2026-10-20-rides/research.md` has no Testing Conventions section. Its Summary says only "pytest only, no browser harness". Everything else is inferred from the existing tests: plain `test_<behavior>` functions, one assert each, inline dict rides, a fixed `TODAY`. There is no `.claude/wb/testing.md`. Drift: none recorded. The 5hz.3 test-writer report says "there was no plan research", but research.md exists. It just has no testing section.
Uncommitted changes: `docs/plans/2026-10-20-rides/tasks.md` was modified (the "Modified Files (Phase 1)" section was rewritten). It was not dirty at the start, and this review did not make the change. It is a plan document, not a test, and is outside the review.

### Integrity
Findings: 3 (0 escalated)
- Source: the Test Integrity comments from the task verifiers on tmp_niHSfpp8MW-5hz.2 (2 findings, 0 escalated) and tmp_niHSfpp8MW-5hz.3 (1 finding, 0 escalated). Task 5hz.4 has no comments and made no changes.
- Note: 5hz.2 cleared its finding at `tests/test_store.py:25` because sibling tests anchor the result. This review reports the same line as a Rewrite (see Findings). The skill requires the presence anchor in the test itself, and a planted defect shows the test passes on an empty result.

### Criterion Coverage
No red commits were supplied, so neither criterion has an outer test. The inner tests that guard each one run at the stated observed-at level (a plain function call):
- 1 (Window): `tests/test_store.py:18` (Oct 1, listed) and `tests/test_store.py:23` (Sep 30, omitted), at `list_rides` level. Both green at HEAD. Planted defects: `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` is caught by :20 only, and a cutoff without the `- 1` is caught by :25 only.
- 2 (Rounding): `tests/test_view_model.py:8` (12.25), `:16` (2.25), `:20` (1.15), `:25` (10.0), `:12` (5), at `format_distance` level. All green at HEAD. Planted defects:
  - `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` is caught by :9 and :17.
  - `ROUND_HALF_DOWN` is caught by :9, :17 and :22.
  - `Decimal(km)` without `str` is caught by :22.
  - `.normalize()` is caught by :26.
  - Disabling the int branch is caught by :13.
  - Every one failed on an assertion.

### Findings
These are proposals. No test was created, edited, or deleted.

- **Verdict**: Rewrite
  - **Rubric item**: Part 1 item 4 (a negative assertion with no positive presence anchor)
  - **Location**: `tests/test_store.py:25` - `assert list_rides([too_old], TODAY) == []`
  - **Evidence type**: deterministic (planted defect)
  - **Objective evidence**: In a disposable worktree of HEAD, I changed `rides/store.py` to `return []`. `test_omits_a_ride_from_28_days_ago` still passed, while :10, :20 and :31 failed. On its own, the test cannot tell "Sep 30 excluded" from "nothing listed". One fix: put an in-window ride (for example Oct 1) in the same input and assert the result equals `[that ride]`. The test then pins both sides of the boundary.
  - **Criterion**: 1 (Window)

none

- `tests/test_view_model.py:9` and `:17`: 12.25 and 2.25 are both exact binary halves. In the five planted rounding defects, both were killed by exactly the same defects (HALF_EVEN, HALF_DOWN). Judgment-only (Specific; overlap).
- Criterion 1, observed at: design.md words this as "The rides page lists a ride from 27 days before today…". The given observed-at is `list_rides`, which the tests meet. Nothing tests `render_rides_page` (`rides/views.py:6`), so a page-level wiring break would not be caught. Judgment-only (Predictive; level).

### Detectors
- Tools run:
  - pytest 9.1.1 on the changed files: 11 passed.
  - `--durations=5`: all tests under 5 ms.
  - Grep heuristics on `tests/test_store.py` and `tests/test_view_model.py` for sleeps and wall clock, mocks and patches, skip, xfail and focus markers, and expected values computed with production helpers (`WINDOW_DAYS`, `Decimal`, `round(`, `format_distance` on both sides): no matches.
  - Assertion-free tests (Python heuristic): 5 tests and 5 asserts in test_store.py, 6 tests and 6 asserts in test_view_model.py, one per test, so none are assertion-free.

- No detector in this stack: assertion-free tests, sleeps, mocking beyond the seam, and copied setup. These were covered by the heuristics above, judgment-only. No doubles appear in either file. not configured

- Outer-test checks (red commit, observed-at level, unchanged since red): no red commits, because the plan predates acceptance criteria.
- Ruff static selection: ruff is not installed in the project.
- Seeded random order: pytest-randomly is not installed.
- First planted-defect attempt: the permission system denied a loop that planted several store defects in one call. I reran each defect as its own call, which established the same results.

Outside the range and not reviewed: `tests/test_store.py:15` (`== []`) and `tests/test_today_page.py:8` (`"x" not in body`) are older negative assertions with the same missing-anchor shape. Every worktree used for planted defects was removed, and `git worktree list` shows only the main tree.

Phase 1 is implemented and verified. Per the run instructions, I've stopped at the checkpoint: the phase milestone is still open and phase 2 has not started.

The plan predates 5.0.0, so it has no acceptance criteria. That means no outer tests were written and no `red(AC-n)` commits exist. Workers still left all test changes to test-writer, and each verifier still checked test integrity.

**Automated checks:**
- **Tests:** `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 13 passed.
- **Syntax:** `python3 -m compileall -q rides tests` is clean.
- **Lint, typecheck, build:** the project has none configured, so none were run.

**Tasks:**
- **`.2` Window to 28 days** (worker on Sonnet, commit `1f25f9e`): `WINDOW_DAYS` changed from 27 to 28. With today = Oct 28, a ride on Oct 1 is listed and one on Sep 30 is not. The verifier passed it after planting 4 defects, and the tests caught every one.
- **`.3` Round half up** (worker on Sonnet, commit `c2de74b`): `format_distance` now rounds half up through `Decimal(str(km))`. 2.25 shows as 2.3 km, 1.15 as 1.2 km, 10.0 stays 10.0 km and 5 stays 5 km. The existing 12.25 expectation was changed from 12.2 to 12.3 km through test-writer, as the plan requires. The verifier passed it after planting 4 defects, and the tests caught every one.
- **`.4` Add tests:** I closed this without a worker. Tasks .2 and .3 had already added every test it lists, so a worker would have had nothing to change; the close reason records which tests and commits cover each item.
- The worker for .2 said the test-writer report it posted on the task was condensed, not word for word. Its verifier confirmed the report still names every change in the diff.

**Test review** (these are proposals; no test was edited):
- **Integrity findings:** 3, none escalated.
- **One finding: rewrite `tests/test_store.py:25`.** The "Sep 30 is omitted" test passes even if `list_rides` returns nothing at all; the reviewer showed this by planting `return []`. The fix is to add an in-window ride to the same input and assert only that ride comes back. I didn't file it as an issue: the filing rule covers only escalated findings and judgment-only findings settled by 2 of 3 reviewers, and this is neither.
- **Majority candidates:** none, so no extra review rounds were needed.
- **Worth a look:**
  - The 12.25 and 2.25 tests may overlap, since they caught exactly the same planted defects. The plan requires both.
  - Nothing tests the rides page itself (`render_rides_page`), so a break between the page and `list_rides` would go uncaught.

**Beads:**
- All Phase 1 tasks are closed: `tmp_niHSfpp8MW-5hz.2`, `.3` and `.4`.
- The milestone `tmp_niHSfpp8MW-5hz.1` has no open blockers and is ready to close once you confirm the manual check.
- A separate commit, `a1689c2`, updates the modified-files section of `tasks.md`.

**Manual check needed** (from tasks.md): open the rides page and confirm it lists the expected rides. A ride from 27 days ago should appear, one from 28 days ago should not, and distances should round half up.

Once you confirm, the remaining steps are: close the milestone, run `/wb:update_status`, add the implementation notes, and save beads state. None of those have been done yet.
